title: Find the best split of a compute budget two ways
brief: Compute the best model size and token count from the closed form, confirm it by searching a grid, and add serving cost to see why a smaller model trained longer can be cheaper overall.
hints: With a = beta / (alpha + beta) and G = (alpha * A / (beta * B)) ** (1 / (alpha + beta)), the best size is N* = G * 6**(-a) * compute**a. Then D* = compute / (6 * N*), so that 6 * N* * D* equals the budget exactly.
grid_optimal builds a log-spaced array of N values, sets D = compute / (6 * N) for each, evaluates predict_loss on the arrays, and takes the N with the smallest loss. np.argmin does the last step.
lifetime_flops adds two bills: 6 * N * D_train for training and 2 * N * served_tokens for answering. Convert to float first so numpy integers cannot wrap around.
